transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. ____. Well, what finally pushed me to come in is... I just keep getting up when I really shouldn't. Like, during sprint planning at work, or even when I'm on important mortgage calls with my husband. I know I need to stay put, but I'll suddenly feel like I desperately need a glass of water, or I'll decide I have to go check something in the other room right that second. Actually, the other room—we're trying to repaint the guest bedroom right now, and picking a color has been a nightmare. My husband wants this sage green, but I feel like green is just so dated, you know? Like those 90s kitchens with the ivy wallpaper. We used to have that in my house growing up, and my mom spent weeks scraping it off. But yeah, I just... I can't seem to stay in my chair when I'm supposed to.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or wired and needed much less sleep than usual?

Wired for days? No, I don't think so. I definitely need my sleep. I mean, I drink a decent amount of coffee, but... no. 

Although, last month we had this massive deployment at work, and I was up until like 3 AM fixing a bug in the API. I was so wired just from staring at the screen and the stress of it all that I couldn't fall asleep right away. I actually ended up watching three episodes of that baking show just to wind down. Have you seen it? The one where they make those crazy illusion cakes? It completely blows my mind how they can make a sponge cake look exactly like a pair of sneakers or a handbag. Like, who even wants to eat a shoe? Plus, fondant tastes absolutely terrible anyway, it's literally just sugar Play-Doh. I always peel it off if I go to a wedding or something. 

But... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, needing less sleep. No, that was just that one night for work. I definitely crashed the next day. I need a solid seven or eight hours usually, or I'm totally useless.
Before age 12, did you have similar problems with fidgeting, getting out of your seat, or trouble staying focused at school?

Oh, definitely. I remember back in elementary school, my teachers were constantly having to move my desk around. They'd put me right up by the chalkboard or off to the side because I was always popping out of my seat. 

Actually, I hated sitting by the chalkboard because of all the chalk dust. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, used to make us go outside and clap the erasers together at the end of the day. Do kids even do that anymore? Probably not, it's all smartboards and iPads now. My niece is in second grade and she literally has her own school-issued iPad. When I was her age, the absolute coolest thing we had was that overhead projector with the clear plastic sheets. I loved when they'd let you write on them with those wet-erase markers. They smelled so weird, kind of like vinegar? I always wanted to buy a pack for myself, but my mom said they'd ruin the walls.

But anyway, yeah, the teachers were always reminding me to stay seated. And I was always blurting things out, talking way before I was actually called on. I'd also just rush through all my worksheets. Like, I understood the work perfectly fine, I really did, I just couldn't slow down to actually do it carefully. I just wanted to get it done so I could... I don't know, go sharpen my pencil for the fifth time or something.
Have you ever had a period when you felt abnormally high, euphoric, or unusually irritable?

No, I've never really had anything like that. I mean, I get irritable sometimes, sure, but just the normal amount. Like when my husband leaves his shoes right in the middle of the hallway. I trip over them constantly. 

I've actually been looking at these shoe storage benches online. They have some really nice ones on Wayfair, but the shipping takes forever. I ordered a rug from them once, and it got lost in transit for three weeks. When it finally arrived, it was the wrong pattern entirely. It was supposed to be this subtle geometric thing, but it looked like a giant kaleidoscope. I ended up putting it in the basement because I didn't want to deal with the return process. The basement is mostly just storage anyway, full of old Halloween decorations and boxes of my college textbooks. I don't know why I keep them, it's not like I'm ever going to read a textbook on introductory microeconomics again. 

But no, to answer your question, no periods of feeling abnormally high or anything like that.
